title: Claim-Driven Verification project state
description: Structural contract for a project's verification.yaml. Describes the document's shape. Semantic obligations -- whether a critical claim actually has covered failure modes, qualified oracles, materially independent evidence, no unresolved conflicts, current evidence and recorded residual uncertainty -- are enforced by the cdv engine and deliberately are NOT expressible here. A document can be valid against this schema and still fail the gate; that is the intended relationship, because the gate is the authority and the schema is only the parser contract.

version.description: Schema version of this document. The engine refuses to evaluate an unsupported version rather than guessing.

project.description: Identifying metadata. Purely informational; never used in a verdict.

state.description: The state under evaluation. Every evidence path is compared against this to establish freshness. Absent or empty state means no evidence can be shown to be current.

commit.description: VCS commit of the evaluated state.

tree_hash.description: Tree or content hash of the evaluated state.

integration.description: Which adapter installed this file and at what version. Written by the installer; used to detect drift between the installed guard and the bootstrap release.

oracles.description: Definitions of the mechanisms that actually decide pass or fail. Every oracle named by a failure mode or an evidence path must appear here.

claims.description: The completion claims. Each is an explicit, testable statement about the system.

conflicts.description: Recorded evidence conflicts and their root-caused resolutions. A conflict detected by the engine that is not resolved here blocks the claim; majority voting is never used.

between.description: Exactly the two evidence ids that disagreed. A resolution that does not name both parties does not match the conflict.

status.description: RESOLVED is the only value that permits the claim to pass.

re_run_evidence.description: Evidence collected after the correction. It must exist in the claim and have result PASS.

independence_exceptions.description: Documented waivers of the two-materially-independent-paths requirement. A waiver is recorded as residual uncertainty and never lowers any other obligation.

criticality_exceptions.description: Reviews permitting a claim that matches a criticality trigger to be handled as NON_CRITICAL. Even with a complete entry, the critical rule set is applied, so the relabelling cannot reduce the evidence bar.

kind.description: How far the oracle stands from the producing system. internal is the producer's own account of itself and can never be the load-bearing evidence for a claim about the world.

qualification.description: Evidence that the oracle itself works. Required for every oracle carrying a critical claim. The known-bad case is the load-bearing half: an oracle never shown to reject a wrong result is not evidence. Two modes exist and are NOT interchangeable. EXECUTED means the engine ran both cases and observed the results. DECLARED means the project asserts they were run; it is auditable and far better than nothing, but it is an assertion about the verifier made by the party that benefits from the verifier passing, so it requires a rationale, a statement of why executing is unavailable, and it produces an explicit assurance downgrade on the claim. The two are kept distinct in every output.

mode.description: EXECUTED: cdv runs both commands and reads the markers from their output; requires --allow-execute-oracles, and is refused rather than downgraded if execution is not permitted. DECLARED: both cases are asserted. The v1.0.0 spelling 'executable' is accepted and means EXECUTED.

rationale.description: Required for DECLARED. At least 40 characters. Why the cases are declared rather than executed.

executable_unavailable_because.description: Required for DECLARED. At least 40 characters. Why executing the oracle is not technically possible. A critical claim may not rely on a declared oracle without this, because the engine cannot otherwise distinguish 'cannot execute' from 'chose not to'.

executable_feasible.description: Set true only to state that execution WAS technically possible and was not done. This is refused: a critical claim must not rely on the weaker mode when the stronger one was available.

result.description: DETECTED means the oracle rejected a deliberately incorrect result.

positive_command.description: Only honoured in EXECUTED mode. Must exit 0 and print a line starting CDV_ORACLE_POSITIVE=PASS. Declaring EXECUTED without both commands is refused as a masquerade.

negative_command.description: Only honoured in EXECUTED mode. Must exit 0 and print a line starting CDV_ORACLE_NEGATIVE=DETECTED. A non-zero exit is a refusal to qualify, not a detection: an oracle that crashes instead of reporting is not trusted.

oracle.description: The oracle that decides whether this failure mode occurred. A failure mode without an oracle has nothing determining its outcome.

dimensions.description: Recorded provenance of an evidence path. Independence is computed from these by comparing pairs; it is never self-declared. model, implementation and runtime form the generation axis; data_source, observation_channel and specification_source form the observation axis. Two paths are materially independent only if they differ on BOTH axes. tool is recorded for audit and never counts toward independence.

evidence_type.description: Free-form tag naming the conventional mechanism that produced this evidence (unit test, e2e, visual, mutation, fault-injection, readback, ...). Conventional testing is not replaced; it is organised under claims.

failure_modes.description: Which failure modes this path covers. When omitted, coverage is inferred from the oracle. Coverage is the only thing that makes evidence count toward a claim.

observed_state.description: What state this evidence was observed against. Compared with the top-level state to establish freshness.

reuse_across_states.description: Only honoured for NON_CRITICAL claims. For a CRITICAL claim, evidence about a different state is not weak evidence, it is not evidence.

statement.description: What is being claimed, in terms that can be falsified.

type.description: Guidance vocabulary, not a closed taxonomy. An unrecognised value is rejected rather than guessed at.

criticality.description: Explicit classification. Defaults conservatively: a claim whose own text matches a criticality trigger is handled with the critical rule set regardless of the value written here.

producer.description: Name of the component whose self-report must not be the sole proof of an external effect.

requires_temporal.description: Force temporal obligations even when type is not TEMPORAL.

requires_world_verification.description: Force external-effect obligations even when type is not OUTCOME.

failure_modes.description: Analysis of how this claim could be true-looking but false. Must precede evidence design.

residual_uncertainty.description: What the evidence does not cover. Required for a critical claim. A single NONE_KNOWN entry is permitted only with a justification.
